name: Hidden Door Sensor
description: A wireless, battery-powered sensor recessed into a door frame that reports when the door opens or closes. It can trigger lights and other Insteon devices.

verification.note: The Hidden Door Sensor Developer Notes name no version or subcategory; the catalog reads the version sold in Europe as the same sensor as the US version, 0x10/0x11, with the same commands.

The Hidden Door Sensor Developer Notes name no version or subcategory; the catalog reads the version sold in Australia and New Zealand as the same sensor as the US version, 0x10/0x11, with the same commands.

steps.text: Remove the battery isolation tab before first use.
Hold the sensor in its intended spot and try linking it to the Hub or a responder to test the location; if linking fails, reposition it or add a Range Extender.
Do all linking now, because installing the sensor covers its SET button.
Choose a spot on the hinge side of the door frame or of the door itself; higher is better for range.
Protect nearby surfaces with masking tape and drill a hole 4 inches deep and 3/4 inch in diameter.
Clean out the shavings and test the fit.
Insert the sensor and fasten it with the included screw.
If the gap between door and frame is too wide to press the contact plunger, slide the spacer over the sensor and fasten it with the provided screw.

notes: Tools: power drill, 3/4-inch spade or auger bit, Phillips screwdriver. Uses one AAA battery.
It also works in casement window frames; for sash windows the Hidden Door Sensor 2845 Owner's Manual recommends Open/Close Sensor 2843.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Hidden Door Sensor beeps.

notes: The first device put into linking mode becomes the controller and the second the responder. Linking mode ends once a link is made.
To control a device: adjust it to the state you want, then press and hold its SET button until it double-beeps.

When already installed (five-tap linking): with the door open, press and release the contact plunger twice, then hold it until the sensor beeps; or with the door closed, open it and press and release the plunger twice, and after a pause the sensor beeps. Repeating five-tap linking cycles between linking, unlinking and exit; the door can be opened or closed while in linking mode.
To add it to a Hub, when the app prompts, press and hold the SET button until the sensor beeps.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Hidden Door Sensor beeps.
Tap the SET button.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking as the responder.
steps.expect: The Hub reports ALL-Linking Completed with the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: While the sensor is still awake, have the Hub send Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20) with cmd2 0x18 (stay awake on).
While the device is still awake, have the Hub send Ping to confirm the link.
Tap the SET button once to finish the scene.
When done, have the Hub send Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20) with cmd2 0x19 (stay awake off) to let the sensor sleep again.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's multi-linking and waking steps and the standard Insteon commands Start ALL-Linking and Ping; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The Hidden Door Sensor Developer Notes give the Link to FF Group option as bit 4 of the operating flags, and say one link with group 0xFF puts a device in every group. That a link made with the SET button covers every group the sensor controls while it's on is read from that; with it off, the button links group 1 only. No document describes adding this product to a Hub.

The device sleeps to save its battery and hears messages only while awake, and no document or observation says it answers Enter Linking Mode (cmd1 0x09); its linking steps put it in linking mode with its own controls.

The Hidden Door Sensor Developer Notes give Set Operating Flags (cmd1 0x20) with cmd2 0x18 for stay awake on and 0x19 for off. Sending it once ALL-Linking Completed gives the device's Insteon ID, while it's still awake, is assembled from this profile's multi-linking and waking steps; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.
Read from the From a Hub alternative to this profile's linking, whose steps are assembled from its own linking steps and standard Insteon commands; no document describes adding this product to a Hub.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Hidden Door Sensor beeps.
Tap the SET button.
Adjust each scene member to its state.
One at a time, press and hold each scene member's SET button until it double-beeps.
Tap the SET button once to finish the scene.

notes: Multi-linking mode lasts 4 minutes or until the SET button is tapped.

steps.text: Press and hold the SET button until the Hidden Door Sensor beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps.

notes: Then press and hold the controlled device's SET button until it double-beeps.

For several devices, tap the SET button after the second beep, press and hold each device's SET button until it double-beeps, then tap the SET button to leave multi-unlinking mode (it also ends after 4 minutes).

steps.text: While the sensor is awake, send Set Operating Flags with cmd2 0x18 (stay awake on) to keep it awake; cmd2 0x19 turns it off.

notes: The Hidden Door Sensor Developer Notes say the sensor sleeps quickly to save battery and must be awake to receive commands; stay awake on uses 0xFF for the awake interval.
The documents don't give a button step to wake the sensor before sending the command.

verification.note: Only the Hidden Door Sensor Developer Notes cover staying awake.

steps.text: Remove the Hidden Door Sensor from the door frame and take out its battery.
Press and hold the SET button while reinstalling the battery.
Keep holding the SET button until the long beep stops.
Release the SET button.

notes: Erases all links and customized properties.

steps.text: Remove the device from every scene, as a controller.

verification.note: Read from how Insteon links work: a device left in a scene keeps links to it in other devices' ALL-Link databases. No document describes removing this product.

steps.text: Remove the device from its scenes first, so no other device keeps links to it.
Press and hold the SET button until the Hidden Door Sensor beeps.
Press and hold the SET button again until it beeps.
Have the Hub start ALL-Linking with link code 0xFF (delete), so the device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub.
steps.expect: The device deletes its group 1 link to the Hub, and the Hub reports the device's Insteon ID

steps.text: If the LED is still blinking, tap the SET button until it stops.

verification.note: Assembled from this profile's unlinking steps and the standard Insteon command Start ALL-Linking; no document describes removing this product from a Hub.

notes: Sends closed to group 2 only when set to.
Sends a heartbeat to group 4 every 24 hours by default. Software can set it to 5 to 1275 minutes, in 5-minute steps.
Sends low battery to group 3 each time it wakes while its battery is below a level software sets.
Sends low battery and heartbeat only when it has links in those groups.
Its heartbeat and low battery messages carry cmd1 0x11 while the door is open and 0x13 while it's closed.
Its Developer Notes give the heartbeat as every 24 hours by default; other sources give 256 times 5 minutes, about 21 hours.
Its owner's manual says the sensor sends its heartbeat once every 24 hours by default.
